{{Quote|Awaud was appalled, and became the leader of the Return&mdash;a movement that urged Mandalorians to defend Mandalorian Space. In 1051 BBY he took the name Mandalore the Uniter. Under his leadership, Mandalorian Space not only survived the upheaval of the New Sith Wars but thrived, emerging as a regional industrial power and protector of neighboring systems and sectors.|Vilnau Teupt, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
'''Mandalore the Uniter''' was the title adopted by the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] '''Aga Awaud''' when he became the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]] of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture during the final [[Standard century/Legends|century]] of the [[New Sith Wars]]. In [[1058 BBY]], he returned to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] and discovered that the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-wide [[Candorian plague/Legends|Candorian plague]] epidemic had [[Death/Legends|killed]] his family and most of [[Clan Awaud/Legends|Clan Awaud]] and that raiders and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] endangered [[Starship/Legends|starship]] travel through [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]].

[[1051 BBY|Seven years]] later, Awaud became the leader, or Mandalore, of his people and began the [[Return (Mandalorian)|Return]] movement that aimed to recall Mandalorians to defend their original [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and its surrounding [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Mandalore the Uniter also initiated reforms in Mandalorian military structure and the manufacture of the culture's traditional [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|armor]]. Under his rule and that of his successor Mandalores, Mandalorian Space became a powerful and influential regional entity offering protection to neighboring [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], and his legacy in the Mandalorian history and culture eventually endured for more than one [[Millennium/Legends|thousand years]].

==Biography==
===A new leader===
{{Quote|In 1058 BBY a mercenary named Aga Awaud returned to Mandalore to find that the Candorian plague had killed his family and most of his clan&mdash;and Mandalorian ships had to band together in caravans through Mandalorian Space, fearing raiders from the lawless surrounding sectors.|Vilnau Teupt, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] who would eventually be known as Mandalore the Uniter was originally a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] named Aga Awaud who lived during the final [[Standard century/Legends|century]] of the [[New Sith Wars]]<ref name="EGTW" /> of [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000 BBY]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> A member of [[Clan Awaud/Legends|Clan Awaud]], he had a family on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="EGTW" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that was the original home of the Mandalorian warrior culture.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> By [[1060 BBY]], Mandalore had fallen victim to<ref name="History">{{SW|url=news/the-history-of-mandalorian-armor|text=The History of Mandalorian Armor|int=The History of Mandalorian Armor|nolive=1}}</ref> the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-wide [[Candorian plague/Legends|Candorian plague]] outbreak, with Awaud's family and most of his clan being among the [[Death/Legends|casualties]]. In addition, fear of raiders<ref name="EGTW" /> and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]]<ref name="History" /> from the lawless [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] surrounding [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]] forced Mandalorian [[Starship/Legends|starships]] to group together into caravans for travel through that region. When Awaud returned to Mandalore in [[1058 BBY]], he was appalled by the fate of his kin and the state of Mandalorian-controlled [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="EGTW" />

[[File:Mandalore_sector.jpg|thumb|left|310px|Mandalore the Uniter led a resurgence of Mandalorian Space (Mandalore sector borders in 0 ABY depicted).]]
In [[1051 BBY]], in an unexpected turn of Mandalorian history, the mercenary became [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]], leader of the Mandalorian people,<ref name="EGTW" /> and initiated the [[Return (Mandalorian)|Return]],<ref name="History" /> a movement that encouraged Mandalorians,<ref name="EGTW" /> including the most capable members of the culture,<ref name="BHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> from throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] to return to Mandalorian Space and defend it.<ref name="EGTW" /> Mandalore the Uniter formed a new [[Mandalorian shock trooper|shock trooper]] order that would rely on speed and surprise during attacks and be more mobile than the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]]<ref name="BHC" /> of the [[3976 BBY]]&ndash;[[3960 BBY]] [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="TEA" /> To achieve that, the Mandalore restarted mass production of the traditional [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]]<ref name="BHC" /> and split it into separate, lighter components<ref name="History" /> in order not to overburden the [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] supplies of the [[Soldier/Legends|warriors']] [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpacks]].<ref name="BHC" /> The general composition of Mandalore the Uniter's [[Armor/Legends|armor]] would eventually become the basis for that worn as late as during<ref name="History" /> the [[Second Imperial Civil War]] that began in [[137 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Under the Uniter and the strong Mandalores who followed him, our homeworld became the protector of many star systems and the center of an honorable civilization.|Tor Vizsla, ''Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad''|<ref name="BHC" />}}
[[File:DeathWatchArmor-BHC.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Mandalorian armor introduced by Mandalore the Uniter served as the basis for that used throughout the subsequent millennium (Death Watch armor depicted).]]
Under the leadership of Mandalore the Uniter<ref name="EGTW" /> as well as the strong Mandalores who succeeded him,<ref name="BHC" /> Mandalorian Space thrived and became a regional industrial power, with the Mandalorians offering protection services to<ref name="EGTW" /> many<ref name="BHC" /> neighboring [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and sectors. Over the subsequent centuries, the culture grew in power and influence to the point where the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] came to view it as a threat, which ultimately led to [[Mandalorian Excision|disastrous consequences]] for the Mandalorians and deep factional divides in their society.<ref name="EGTW" />

A [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]] after the reign of Mandalore the Uniter, his role in the resurgence of the Mandalorian people and the evolution of their armor was noted in ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', a manifesto of the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] Mandalorian splinter group. The document was supposedly [[Author/Legends|written]] by the movement's [[Secret Mandalore|leader]], [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;although the Death Watch's opponent [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] doubted its authenticity&mdash;and was eventually included in the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]'' by Jango's [[Gender/Legends|son]], the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="BHC" /> [[Vilnau Teupt]] similarly mentioned Mandalore the Uniter<ref name="EGTW" />&mdash;whose clan had survived<ref name="Friends">''[[Friends Like These]]''</ref> for at least one thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]]<ref name="EGTW" /> by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]<ref name="Friends" />&mdash;and his role in Mandalorian history in the keynote address "[[Industry, Honor, Savagery: Shaping the Mandalorian Soul]]" at [[Brentaal Academy]]'s [[Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History]] in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|The Uniter's armor remains the basis for that worn by the Faithful today.|Tor Vizsla, ''Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad''|<ref name="BHC" />}}
Mandalore the Uniter wore a set of Mandalorian armor. It included a [[Helmet/Legends|helmet]]; torso, shoulder, and [[Limb/Legends|forearm]] plates; and a [[Belt/Legends|belt]] with several pouches. The paint pattern of the armor plates consisted of irregular light lines against the backdrop of the darker armor itself. The back section of the Mandalore's armor included several vertical spikes.<ref name="BHC" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Aga Awaud is a new character&mdash;I wanted another transitional figure, one who would be remembered by Mandalorians of many political stripes later, and celebrated by them. (His story would be an interesting one as well.)|Jason Fry|<ref name="Endnotes PT4">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/21728447315/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-4|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 4}}</ref>}}
[[File:Essential_Guide_to_Warfare-cover.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Mandalore the Uniter was introduced in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.]]
Mandalore the Uniter was introduced in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]. In the book, the character is described in a section also mentioning [[Mandalore the Ultimate]], who transformed the Mandalorian society into one including members of many different [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="EGTW" /> while also ultimately becoming<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-2-ancient-coruscant|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 2 - Ancient Coruscant}}</ref> generally<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> known as the last Mandalore who was a [[Taung/Legends|Taung]]&mdash;a member of the original Mandalorian species.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> Fry later noted that Mandalore the Uniter had been created as another transitional Mandalorian leader whose memory would have been celebrated by later Mandalorians of various [[Politics/Legends|political]] affiliations.<ref name="Endnotes PT4" />

When Fry was asked on the [[Jedi Council Forums]] of [[TheForce.net]] whether the use of the title of "Mandalore the Uniter" in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' had been a reference to<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/50044846|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Guide to Warfare by Jason Fry and a pseudonymous Scotsman|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2012-09-19|time=12:57 PM|quote=Re Mandalore the Uniter, it was an accident. But a lucky accident. NT and the Mercs are awesome folks, and I'm very glad it worked out the way it did.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802142556/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-by-jason-fry-and-a-pseudonymous-scotsman.30937840/page-108#post-50044846}} {{C|In response to: "When you have a moment, I was wondering if the new Mandalore you introduced in ''Warfare'', Mandalore the Uniter, was given that title as an intentional nod to Novall Talon, leader of the Mandalorian Mercs."}}</ref> the [[Wikipedia:Cosplay|cosplay]] character of the same name&mdash;used since [[2008]]&mdash;portrayed by [[Tom Hutchens]], the founder of the [[Mandalorian Mercs|Mandalorian Mercs Costume Club]],<ref name="MandaloreTheUniter">{{WebCite|url=https://mandaloretheuniter.com|text=Mandalore the Uniter|work=[https://mandaloretheuniter.com mandaloretheuniter.com]|archivedate=20230923041441}}</ref> the author admitted that the similarity was a "lucky accident" while also praising that organization and expressing satisfaction at the unintentional connection.<ref name="JCF" /> Hutchens was involved in the creation of<ref name="MandaloreTheUniterAbout">{{WebCite|url=https://mandaloretheuniter.com/about|text=About - Mandalore the Uniter|work=[https://mandaloretheuniter.com mandaloretheuniter.com]|archivedate=20230605210504}}</ref> [[Daniel Wallace]]'s [[2013]] reference book ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', in which the official Mandalore the Uniter was illustrated<ref name="BHC" /> by [[Mark McHaley]].<ref name="History" />
